findings.title: Validate the destination before debiting the source
findings.explanation: For a transfer with sufficient funds to an existing account whose ID begins with `locked-`, current head subtracts `cents` from the source and then throws `destination locked`. The destination is never credited, so a rejected transfer still changes the ledger. No rollback exists in the changed function. Restore the lock validation before either balance mutation and add a regression assertion that both balances remain unchanged after rejection.
findings.failurePath: `transfer` resolves both accounts and passes the funds check, debits `from.balanceCents`, detects the locked destination, and throws before crediting `to.balanceCents`; the caller observes failure while the source retains the debit.

candidates.invariant: Transfer validation must complete before either account balance is mutated.
candidates.counterexample: With sufficient funds and a destination whose ID starts with "locked-", the source balance is decremented and then the function throws, leaving the transfer partially applied.
candidates.evidenceNeeded: Confirm the transfer contract or tests require rejected transfers to leave both account balances unchanged; reproduce with a locked destination and inspect state after the exception.

candidates.invariant: An exception during transfer must not leave persistent in-memory state partially mutated.
candidates.counterexample: The moved destination-lock check throws after the debit, so callers receive an error while the source account has already lost the funds.
